Playbook.name: AD — Repeated Authentication Against Disabled or Locked Accounts - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Credential Access / Valid Accounts abuse attempt

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: One source produced 10+ authentication attempts against DISABLED, LOCKED or EXPIRED accounts (4771 0x12; 4625 substatus 0xC0000072/0xC0000234/0xC0000193) in 30 minutes. Triage question: is someone replaying stolen-but-dead credentials or enumerating former staff, or is an orphaned system still trying its old account?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Attackers replaying breached credential dumps hit disabled ex-employee accounts first; the same shape is produced by decommissioned-but-running services. The wrong verdict either misses recon or wastes IR time.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: Dead-account auth burst
Signal.Details: >= 10 failures with disabled/locked/expired statuses from one source in the window.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Source IP producing the dead-account authentication attempts.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Orphaned service: ONE dead service account, steady cadence - lean Misconfiguration.
Multiple different disabled HUMAN accounts (ex-staff) from one source - treat as credential-replay recon, escalate.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether $source_ip is replaying dead credentials across accounts (attack) or is an orphaned system using its own expired identity (ops).

Step.name: Which dead accounts, which statuses, what cadence
Step.Purpose: Account mix is the core discriminator: one service account = orphan; several human accounts = replay/enumeration.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND ((event.code == "4771" AND winlog.event_data.Status == "0x12") OR (event.code == "4625" AND winlog.event_data.SubStatus IN ("0xc0000072","0xc0000234","0xc0000193"))) | EVAL reason = CASE(winlog.event_data.SubStatus == "0xc0000072", "disabled", winlog.event_data.SubStatus == "0xc0000234", "locked", winlog.event_data.SubStatus == "0xc0000193", "expired", "krb-0x12") | STATS attempts = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), reasons = VALUES(reason) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | SORT attempts DESC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: Human naming pattern (first/last names) across multiple accounts = replaying a stale credential list. A single svc_*/app account = orphaned automation.

Step.name: Does the same source also authenticate successfully (live credentials too)
Step.Purpose: A source mixing valid logons with dead-account attempts is a real workstation (possibly compromised, or a shared kiosk); a source with ONLY dead attempts is automation or attack infrastructure.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code IN ("4624","4625","4771") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), users = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY event.code | SORT event.code | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: Only failures, several users = replay list. 4624 successes present = live system; check whether the successful account should be associated with the dead ones (same person pre/post rename?).

Step.name: When were these accounts disabled and by whom (recent lifecycle)
Step.Purpose: An account disabled TODAY still being used by its owner's devices is expected residue; accounts disabled long ago being probed is not.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4725","4740","4722") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: If a probed account appears here as freshly disabled (4725), the residue window explains the alert. No recent lifecycle events = the accounts were disabled earlier; probing them now is more suspicious.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows multiple distinct disabled HUMAN accounts probed from one source, and INV-03 shows none of them was disabled today.
Node.Result: True Positive (Credential Replay / Ex-staff Enumeration - escalate)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows the source is otherwise a normally-authenticating workstation AND INV-01 shows exactly one account disabled TODAY (fresh-disable residue from that user's own device).
INV-01 shows one service/application account attempted continuously and the source is an application server.
Source has no valid authentications, targets 2+ dead accounts, but source ownership cannot be established from context.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-DEAD-ACCTS, INV-02-DEAD-MIX, INV-03-DEAD-LIFECYCLE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Expected residue: a just-disabled user's own devices keep retrying briefly.

Indicators.Item: Single account, disabled within the last hours (INV-03).
Source is that user's known workstation.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm with IAM the disable action.
Close as benign_activity; helpdesk optionally clears saved sessions.

TruePositive.Definition: Deliberate use of dead credentials - replaying a breach list or targeting former-staff access.

Indicators.Item: Several distinct disabled human accounts from one source.
Source has no legitimate auth footprint (INV-02 failures only).

SOCAction.Item: Cross-check the probed names against breach-dump monitoring.
Escalate to IR - this is recon of your identity attack surface.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An orphaned system/service still authenticating with its dead account.

Indicators.Item: One svc/app account, steady machine cadence, application-server source.
Continues across days; recurring same-account alerts (suppression 6h).

SOCAction.Item: Identify the process on the source and decommission or re-credential it.
Track under credential-hygiene P0; do not exception.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If replay pattern: block source, notify IR.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Hunt other sources probing the same dead accounts.
Validate the disabled accounts cannot be re-enabled without approval.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Purge stale credentials from decommissioned systems.
Feed confirmed-orphan sources to the ops cleanup list.

QualityChecks.Check: Statuses used: 0x12/0xC0000072/0xC0000234/0xC0000193 - verified live in JCB.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Fresh-disable residue confirmed with IAM and faded out.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Source contained; replay list scope documented; no dead account re-enabled.
